mappings.note: Minicoy in Lakshadweep as the Indian island 130 km from the Maldives. Location and distance, goal-level CG-SST1; LO-4 is climatic regions only.
Garuda on the Indonesian rupiah, Vishnu's vahana carried into a national symbol. Cultural transmission surviving into the present, goal-level CG-SST2.

Assertion-reason: Thai culture shows Indian influence because monks, scholars and texts travelled maritime routes from the 3rd century BCE. The reason is the transmission of a religious movement, LO-12; CG-SST2 is not added because the reason clause is explicitly religious.
Oman as India's closest Gulf defence partner, first to exercise with all three services. Goal-level CG-SST4 for a state-to-state relationship; the frame carries no defence or foreign-policy outcome.
A traditional neighbour as one sharing a land boundary - the counterpart definition to the maritime-neighbour items. Goal-level CG-SST1.
Recall of the 15,100 km land boundary. Spatial extent, goal-level CG-SST1.
Names Sri Lanka and the Maldives as immediate maritime neighbours. Location, goal-level CG-SST1.
Buddhism as the religion linking India and China. Transmission of a religious movement, LO-12.
Dates Buddhism's arrival in China to around the 1st century CE. Chronology of a religious movement's spread, LO-12.
India's chief exports to China - iron ore, chemicals, cotton yarn. Bilateral trade composition, goal-level CG-SST4; C-SST4.2 is local markets only.
Pakistan founded on a religious basis. A fact about Partition, so goal-level CG-SST2; LO-12 is rejected because no religious idea or movement is being explained, only a political founding principle.
Dates the Kargil War to 1999. Modern historical chronology, goal-level CG-SST2, whose competencies stop at medieval India.
The Kartarpur Corridor as a visa-free crossing. Goal-level CG-SST4, matching the other Kartarpur items.
Bangladesh born in 1971. Historical chronology, goal-level CG-SST2.

The Sundarban as the World Heritage Site shared by India and Bangladesh. LO-8 for the joint conservation of flora and fauna; LO-6 is reserved here for the items that make its cyclone-barrier function explicit.
Pashupatinath as the Kathmandu pilgrimage temple. Competency-level C-SST2.3: a living religious tie, where LO-11 would need architecture and LO-12 a movement.
Guru Padmasambhava as the bringer of Vajrayana to Bhutan. The arrival of a religious school, LO-12.
Burma as Myanmar's earlier name. A historical renaming, goal-level CG-SST2; CG-SST1 is rejected because nothing spatial is asked.
Uttarapatha as the route from the Ganga plains through Afghanistan to Central Asia. An ancient trade route, goal-level CG-SST2; no LO covers historical routes.
Suvarnabhumi as the 'golden land'. Historical naming, goal-level CG-SST2.
Expands SAARC. An intergovernmental body, goal-level CG-SST4.
Names the Palk Strait between India and Sri Lanka. Location, goal-level CG-SST1.
Dhivehi's borrowings from Sanskrit, Prakrit, Tamil, Malayalam and Hindi. Linguistic evidence of long contact, goal-level CG-SST2.
The ancient name of Singapore, Singapuram. Historical naming, goal-level CG-SST2. (The stored answer for this row is a watermark line followed by unrelated Silk Route text; see report.)
Chabahar's significance as India's route to Afghanistan and Central Asia. A state trade and transport project, goal-level CG-SST4.
Copper ingots as the evidence for Harappan-Oman trade over 5,000 years ago. Archaeological evidence, goal-level CG-SST2.
Long answer on Buddhism as the bridge to China, Bhutan and beyond, with Xuanzang and Padmasambhava named. Spread of a religious movement, LO-12.
India-Pakistan complexity: shared pre-1947 history and Partition (CG-SST2) set against wars, tension and the Kartarpur Corridor (CG-SST4). Both registers are required by the model answer.
India-Bangladesh interdependence through a long border and the transboundary Ganga and Brahmaputra (CG-SST1, resources across space) plus joint protection of the Sundarban (LO-8).
The 1950 Treaty as the basis of open borders, integration of border communities and India's position as Nepal's largest trade partner. Goal-level CG-SST4.
Maritime routes carrying Indian culture to Southeast Asia: scripts and epics (CG-SST2) and shared temple architecture such as Angkor Wat (LO-11). Both are cited in the model answer.
India-Afghanistan across time: the Uttarapatha and Afghanistan as a Buddhist centre (CG-SST2), then present-day Indian infrastructure support (CG-SST4).
The 2018 Land Border Crossing Agreement easing movement and trade with Myanmar. A bilateral instrument, goal-level CG-SST4.
How India and Afghanistan were historically linked - the Uttarapatha and centuries of exchange. Goal-level CG-SST2 alone, unlike the longer item above, because no contemporary strand is asked for.
SAARC's purpose: shared socio-cultural and economic progress across South Asia. Goal-level CG-SST4.

Sri Lanka's civil war between the Sinhalese majority and Tamil minority driving refugees into Tamil Nadu. A modern conflict and its demographic consequence; goal-level CG-SST2, since no LO covers conflict or displacement.
India's relief to the Maldives during the 2004 tsunami, the 2014 Male water crisis and COVID-19. Disaster response, LO-6.
Maldivian vulnerability to a one-metre sea-level rise. Competency-level C-SST1.3: the question tests exposure to a hazard, whereas LO-6 asks for preventive action and LO-8 for conservation behaviour.
Dvaravati from Dvaraka and Ayutthaya from Ayodhya. Cultural transmission in place names, goal-level CG-SST2.
The Trilateral Highway improving connectivity and regional trade. A state infrastructure project, goal-level CG-SST4.
Indian influence on the Malay Peninsula: the Srivijaya name and a Brahmi-derived script. Cultural and linguistic transmission, goal-level CG-SST2.

Singapore's 9 percent Indian-origin population alongside its position as a major investor in India. The economic strand dominates, so goal-level CG-SST4 rather than the CG-SST2 used for the Tamil-language items.
India-Indonesia cooperation in regional groupings on trade, maritime security and defence. Goal-level CG-SST4; the disaster-relief clause is one item in a list, so LO-6 is not added.
Why the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre exists - to alert India and neighbours to seafloor earthquakes. Preventive action against disaster, LO-6.

Stem asks how India and Iran were historically connected; mapped on the stem as ancient land and sea contact, goal-level CG-SST2. (The stored answer for this row is an advertising line plus a case-study fragment belonging to a different question; see report.)

This row's stem is two questions run together, and the scored content is the Bhutan case study its answer resolves: a hydroelectric plant generating power for Bhutan and export to India. LO-8 for renewable energy and shared water, CG-SST4 for the bilateral project. (Merged stem; see report.)
Case study identifying a copper ingot from Oman in an Indus city and what it proves about maritime trade 5,000 years ago. Archaeological inference, goal-level CG-SST2.

Case study on nations pooling sensors after the 2004 tsunami, resolving to the Hyderabad warning centre. LO-6 for the preventive system; CG-SST4 for part (c), which asks how the initiative reflects regionalism.
India as the Indian Ocean's first responder, evidenced by Maldives relief in 2004, 2014 and during COVID-19. Disaster response, LO-6.
The 2004 tsunami's effect on regional cooperation, producing the sensor and satellite network. LO-6; CG-SST4 is not added because the answer stays on the warning system rather than on institutions.

The Ramayana in Southeast Asian arts, literature and royal ceremony, with Thai monarchs named Rama. Cultural transmission, goal-level CG-SST2; LO-11 is rejected because the sculptures are cited as narrative, not as construction technique.
India-Iran across time: Bronze Age land and sea contact (CG-SST2) and the Chabahar investment today (CG-SST4).
Case study on a trader in the Maldives noticing Dhivehi's Indian vocabulary and familiar food. Centuries of maritime cultural exchange, goal-level CG-SST2.
Case study of a Kathmandu student crossing daily into Bihar, resolving to the 1950 Treaty and its socio-economic benefits. Goal-level CG-SST4, matching the other open-border items.

Which religion travelled from India's shores to Indonesia - keyed as Islam, carried by Indian Ocean traders. LO-12 for the transmission of a religious tradition; the key is worth a second look given the chapter's Hindu-Buddhist emphasis (see report).
Borobudur as the world's largest Buddhist monument. Identification of a religious monument, LO-11.
The Avesta as the Zoroastrian text paralleling the Rigveda. Two ancient textual traditions, goal-level CG-SST2, consistent with the earlier Avesta item.
Locates Chabahar in Iran. Bare location, so goal-level CG-SST1 here, unlike the Chabahar significance items which carry CG-SST4.
Contrasts a land-bordered neighbour with one reached across a shared sea. The chapter's core spatial distinction, goal-level CG-SST1.
The Indian Ocean carrying half the world's container traffic and two-thirds of its oil. CG-SST1 for the spatial distribution of routes and resources, CG-SST4 for the trade that flows on them.
